So I bought myself an mvp 3.0 60w and am loving the shit out of it so far. I have a kanger subtank on it and a helios rba that I use every once in a while. I build my kanger to about 1.8 ohms and I can't really go over 25w without getting a burnt taste. My question is what kind of build can take high wattage (I've seen some mods go up to 100W+) and what advantage does this have over mechanical mods if any?

Well ya see, high ohms like that don't require as much Wattage for the same amount of voltage. SO, that means that you can go lower on wattage and still get a great vape.

That being said, Try building a nice clean coil around .5 ohms instead and see how that fairs. If you're going to do that, make sure you have good wicking, I recommend the scottish roll technique so that you get as much juice as possible without overdripping.

Myself, on my tanks like the subtank, or my favorite the goliath, I do a dual coil, about 11 wraps on a 3/32 drill bit, and 30 watts gets me an amazing vape.

HOpe that helps!

Lower gauge (thicker) wires will also handle higher wattages better! It all comes down to whether your wicking can keep up with the wattage output you're looking for. You won't get 100W off a Subtank, but 30W should be easily accomplished!

The biggest advantage regulated mods have over mechanicals are:

  • You don't have to worry about battery safety - the likelihood a regulated will blow up on you relative to a mechanical is infinitesimal.

  • You get a consistent vape until the battery dies. With mechanicals, they die fairly quickly over the course of the battery's charge, and you can feel it decrease in power.

Regulated mods come in all shapes and sizes, too. None of them will be quite as small as a lot of mechanicals, but you can always find something that fits into your aesthetic!
